title: canary-communication-and-behavioral-playbook-wip
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook about the human side of canaries and A/B rollouts — how we communicate risk, set expectations, and structure stakeholder behavior to reduce confusion and speed decisions. Focus is product+ops+cs+engineering handoffs (cross-functional). Not a replacement for the technical runbooks; this complements them with messaging, cadence, and psychology-informed rituals.

Audience:
- Product managers owning feature hypotheses
- SRE/Oncall who will watch the canary
- Solutions/CS for customer comms if needed
- Executives for escalation framing
- Engineering owners for rollbacks/fallbacks

Key principles (short):
1) Signal clarity over information overload — pick 2 primary KPIs and call them out in every update.
2) Decision cadence beats prediction — schedule short decision checkpoints before letting the canary expand.
3) Socialize the fallback BEFORE the canary: peoples' readiness to rollback increases if they already agreed on the metric and action.
4) Make the cost of waiting visible — estimates on user impact and cost of delay help push timely rollbacks.
5) Preserve trust with transparent comms; avoid surprise silent rollbacks.

Pre-canary checklist (owner: PM + Eng lead):
- Define primary success/failure metrics (max 2). Example: median p99 latency for model inference, and weekly normalized task success rate.
- Define secondary guardrails (error spike, token cost delta > 30%, model hallucination rate).
- Establish exact rollback triggers (numeric thresholds + hold window).
- Decide exposure slices (cohort percentages and selection criteria).
- Stakeholder map: who needs real-time Slack notifications, who needs hourly digests, who only gets post-mortem.
- Pre-approved rollback authority: name(s) who can trigger immediate rollback without full meeting.
- Draft Slack templates for canary start/expand/pause/rollback.

Suggested Slack templates (copy-paste friendly):
- Canary start: [CANARY] Starting canary for <feature> -> 2% traffic to variant B. Owners: @eng-owner, @pm. Primary KPIs: latency(ms), success_rate(%). Monitoring dashboard: <link>. Expected window: 2h.
- Canary pause/observe: [CANARY] Pausing expansion: observed latency delta > 2x baseline at p95. Holding at 2% while we investigate. Owners investigating: @eng-owner.
- Canary rollback: [CANARY] Rolling back variant B to baseline for all traffic due to sustained p95 latency > threshold for 20 minutes. Postmortem triage: <link>.

Communication cadence recommendation:
- T0 (start): immediate Slack post to ops/product/exec/biz stakeholders with KPIs and links.
- T+15m: ops-only check-in if any anomalies, otherwise no message.
- T+60m: short update on Slack summarizing trends against primary KPIs.
- Decision checkpoint (pre-agreed): at 2h / or after N requests whichever first. Live decision meeting only if threshold crossed; otherwise expand.
- Post-expand: summary to broader audience with what was observed and next steps.

Behavioral nudges and templates:
- Commitment device: ask stakeholders to sign off (emoji react) on rollback authority and thresholds before canary. This reduces “analysis paralysis.”
- Pre-mortem prompt: before start, ask: 'What three things would make us rollback in the first hour?' Capture answers and pin them in the thread.
- Contrast framing: present both the cost of immediate rollback and the cost of false-negative (letting bad variant run longer). Use numbers where possible (expected affected users, revenue delta, infra spend).
- Default bias: make the safe path the default in ambiguous cases (e.g., if metrics drift but unclear, default to pause and gather).

Cross-functional responsibilities (short):
- Product: sets hypothesis, primary KPIs, and success criteria.
- Eng: implements rollout controls, dashboards, and rollback. Oncall monitors and escalates.
- SRE: ensures observability and helps interpret infra signals.
- CS/Solutions: prepares customer-facing text if canary touches specific customers.
- Legal/Compliance: get looped in for regulated customer groups before any expansion.

Escalation taxonomy (simple):
- Severity 1 (S1): user-facing outage or data corruption. Immediate rollback, incident channel, exec page.
- Severity 2 (S2): significant metric regression for primary KPI for > 15 minutes. Pause and investigation; PM+Eng decision within 30 minutes.
- Severity 3 (S3): non-critical but measurable drift in secondary KPIs. Monitor and schedule follow-up.

Example scenarios and recommended response (concrete):
1) Latency spike only on p99 but p50 stable: pause expansion, see if spike correlates with error logs or particular customer cohorts. If spike subsides and no errors, resume with slower ramp.
2) Small increase in hallucination/relevance errors for chat assistant: stop expansion, collect sample prompts, run offline A/B comparison, consult applied-ml for quick guard. Consider quick prompt templating roll-forward instead of rollback.
3) Token cost 40% higher but UX unchanged: weigh cost vs retention experiments. If burst is narrow to a cohort, pause expansion and run cost-limited slices while we tweak quantization or model variant.

Postmortem & learning loop:
- Short write-up within 48 hours: summary, timeline, root cause, and owner actions.
- Share with cross-functional stakeholders and ops review meeting.
- Add key metric plots and exemplar inputs (for ML regressions).
- Capture one operating rule change to apply to next canary (e.g., change decision window from 2h to 1h).

Customer-facing messaging guide (if CS needs to notify):
- Keep it simple, non-technical, and specific about impact and timeframe. Avoid model-internal jargon. Example: "We briefly rolled back a new assistant behavior that caused incorrect answers for a small number of requests. We reverted to the prior experience while we fix and will follow up within 48 hours."

Open questions / things to iterate on (todo):
- Optimal decision window for short-lived chat features (1h vs 3h?) — run a small experiment across 4 releases.
- Standardize two KPI buckets across product lines so exec comms are consistent.
- Integrate a simple yes/no rollback button in console for PM+Oncall with auditable logs.
- Design A/B labeling for customers so CS can include clear language when needed.

Notes to self / working fragments:

- Consider psychological safety checklist for engineers who will be asked to rollback morning-of.
- Add a short script for exec readouts: 3 bullet summary, what we did, next steps.

---
